findings.issue_text: [BUG] totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which over-counts by one whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100 members at limit 50 yields totalPages=3 when only 2 pages exist), so showingLast never becomes true on the real last page and 'next' navigates to a phantom page whose offset (clamped to user_count) returns an empty member list. An admin viewing a group with 50/100/150... members sees the 'next' arrow enabled on the final populated page, clicks it, and gets a blank member list showing '3/3' with zero members; they must click 'previous' to get back to real data.

[BUG] The item view template tests {{#unless automatic}}, but the view is rendered with the member (Discourse.User) as its context via itemView="group-member" in group.hbs, so `automatic` resolves against the User object (which has no such property) and is always falsy — the remove link renders for members of automatic groups. On automatic groups (admins, etc.) every member row shows the 'x' remove control; an admin who clicks it gets a bootbox confirm, a DELETE that the server rejects with 422 can_not_modify_automatic, and no visible feedback that nothing happened.

[BUG] The redesigned admin form still collects alias_level via the combo-box and the model's asJSON includes it, but the new create action only assigns name and visible (`group.name = ...; group.visible = ...`), so alias_level is silently dropped when creating a group. An admin creates a group with a chosen alias level; the group is persisted with the default alias_level 0, and the setting only takes effect if the admin saves a second time after the group has an id.

[BUG] The server now paginates /groups/:name/members at a default limit of 50 for all groups, and the public group-members route fetches only that first page via model.findMembers(), but members.hbs gains no pagination controls — the public members page is silently truncated to 50 rows. Any group with more than 50 members (previously shown in full, or up to 200 for automatic groups) displays 50 members on the public /groups/:name/members page with no way for a visitor to see the rest — a silent data truncation regression.

[ADVISORY] addMembers and removeMember chain only .then() with no rejection handler, so a 422 from can_not_modify_automatic (or any validation failure on group.save) leaves the UI in its prior state with no client-side indication of failure. Admins clicking 'Add' or the remove 'x' on a group the server refuses get a silent no-op (beyond whatever global ajax error flash Discourse shows); combined with the always-rendered remove control on automatic groups, this produces clicks that appear to do nothing.

[ADVISORY] add_members silently skips usernames that don't resolve to a user (and does not strip whitespace from the comma-split entries), and the new spec drops the old explicit 'succeeds silently when adding non-existent users' verification instead of preserving it as a documented contract. An admin who types ' bob' or a typo'd username into the free-text selector sees a success response and a refreshed list without the intended member, with no indication that any username was ignored.

[ADVISORY] The new pagination logic in GroupsController#members (limit/offset parsing, meta{total,limit,offset} response shape) has no controller spec in this diff, and the previous flat-array response shape is not exercised by any test either. A regression in the meta payload (e.g. dropping `total` or miscomputing offset) or in the limit/offset parsing breaks the admin pagination UI and public consumers with no test failing; the response contract changed shape with zero verification.

[ADVISORY] limit and offset are taken from params via .to_i with no lower bound, so a negative offset (e.g. ?offset=-1) reaches ActiveRecord's limit/offset and PostgreSQL raises on negative OFFSET, producing a 500. The previously automatic-groups-only exposure is now extended to every group: anyone who can reach a visible group's members endpoint can trigger a 500 with a single crafted query parameter.

[ADVISORY] The admin-group-selector component template is gutted to a bare <input type="text"> with no value binding, leaving the component's public surface in place but functionally dead. Any existing or future consumer of {{admin-group-selector}} renders a text input that binds to nothing and has no autocomplete — either an accidental leftover of this rework or an unexplained silent behavior change for out-of-tree callers.

[ADVISORY] addMembers leaves the TODO 'should clear the input' unimplemented, so the user-selector retains its usernames after a successful add. An admin who clicks 'Add' twice (or clicks Add after editing the list) re-submits the same username list; combined with the silent per-username add loop, stale input makes it easy to fire repeated add requests without noticing.

[ADVISORY] The create/update request contract silently changed shape: nested `group` params, `usernames` on create, and the PATCH `changes` incremental-membership protocol were all removed, so existing API consumers now get 422s (create with old `group:` payload yields blank name) or silent no-op successes (PUT/PATCH with old payloads pass no top-level params, `group.save` runs, 200 is returned with nothing applied). Out-of-tree API consumers and scripts that create groups with initial members or patch membership incrementally get success responses while no membership change or group field is applied; there is no deprecation or version bump accompanying this rewrite.

[ADVISORY] The public GET members endpoint changed its response from a bare serialized array to a `{members: [...], meta: {...}}` envelope, breaking every existing consumer of this public JSON shape. Any external consumer or integration parsing `GET /groups/:name/members` as an array now receives an object and breaks; this contract change is bundled into a UI-focused 'fix group memberships' PR with no migration note.

[BUG] totalPages uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which produces a nonexistent page whenever the member count is an exact multiple of the limit (50 members, limit 50 → totalPages 2 while only page 1 exists). The pager renders '1/2' and the enabled next control navigates to offset 50, where the server returns zero members and the admin sees a permanently empty member list until they page back.

[BUG] After removeMember, findMembers clamps the offset against the still-stale client-side `user_count` (it is only updated from the response's meta), so the request goes out with an offset equal to the old count and the server echoes it back in `meta.offset`, leaving the UI on an empty page beyond the new last page. An admin on the last page who removes the final visible member (e.g. 51 members, offset 50, remove the last one) sees an empty list with a pager reading past the real page count; recovery requires manually clicking previous.

[BUG] The rewritten `create` action only assigns `name` and `visible`, but the client's `create()` sends `alias_level` via `asJSON`, so the alias level chosen on the new-group form is silently dropped on creation. An admin who sets an alias level while creating a group gets a group with the default alias level and no error or indication; the setting only takes effect after a subsequent edit-and-save cycle.

[ADVISORY] The new dedicated add_members endpoint still skips usernames that do not resolve to a user and then returns success_json, so a request where every username is mistyped reports success while adding zero members. An admin typing 'bob, fred ' or misspelled names into the new Add-members input sees a success result and a refreshed list without the intended users, with no feedback about which usernames were dropped; for a PR whose stated purpose is 'proper handling of group memberships' this silent-drop behavior is under-scoped.

[ADVISORY] The members action gained non-trivial new behavior (limit/offset pagination, total counting, and a brand-new meta envelope serialized via serialize_data instead of render_serialized) with no spec added anywhere in this diff. A regression in the pagination math, the meta payload shape, or the envelope serialization ships unnoticed; the removed 'TODO: more than 200 groups truncates' workaround is also deleted with no test pinning the new behavior that replaces it.

[ADVISORY] The shared `.form-horizontal` rules (bold labels, 350px inputs, 20px checkboxes) were deleted from their original broader parent selector and re-added only under `.groups, .badges`, so any other admin section that previously matched the old selector silently loses its form styling. Admin pages outside the groups and badges screens (whatever else fell under the original parent block) render with unstyled default-width inputs and labels after this change; the author had to add `.badges` explicitly, which is evidence the old block was serving sections beyond groups.

[ADVISORY] The next/previous actions fire unguarded async `findMembers()` calls with no request serialization, so rapid next-then-previous clicks can have their responses resolve out of order and the last-resolved stale response overwrites `offset`/`members` via setProperties. An admin clicking quickly through the pager sees the wrong member page displayed (page contents and page counter disagree with the actual requested offset) until they click again.

[BUG] totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which produces a phantom empty trailing page whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit. A group with exactly 50 members (limit=50) reports totalPages=2; page 2 requests offset=50 from the server, returns zero rows, and the admin sees an empty member list labeled '2/2' with the next control disabled (showingLast true), unable to get back a populated view without clicking previous. Every group whose membership hits a multiple of the page size shows a blank last page.

[BUG] The public /groups/:name/members response shape silently changed from a bare serialized array to a {members: [...], meta: {...}} envelope, and a hard default limit of 50 was introduced for groups that previously returned their full member list. Existing API consumers and any non-diff client code parsing this public endpoint as a JSON array now receive an object and break; custom groups that previously returned all members (no limit at all in the old code) and automatic groups (default 200) are now silently truncated to 50, and the public group members tab (templates/group/members.hbs) gained no pagination controls, so members beyond the first 50 are unreachable in the UI entirely.

[BUG] The update action dropped both accepted request envelopes without versioning: PUT's params[:group][:usernames] full-membership replacement and PATCH's params[:changes] add/delete form are now silently ignored while the endpoint still returns 200. Existing API consumers (admin-key scripts) that PUT group[usernames]=... to sync membership or PATCH changes[add]/changes[delete] for incremental updates get a success response but no membership change occurs — name/visible still apply, so the caller cannot even detect the no-op. PATCH requests additionally fall into the PUT code path, so the changes payload is dropped without error.

[BUG] The create action changed its accepted envelope from nested params[:group][:name]/[:usernames]/[:visible] to flat params[:name]/[:visible], silently discarding the usernames field. Existing API consumers posting group[name]=x&group[usernames]=a,b get a 200 with a created group that has none of the requested members — the old create seeded membership atomically with creation and this behavior is gone with no error or version bump, so callers believe members were added.

[ADVISORY] remove_member mutates membership through the raw association (group.users.delete(user_id)) while add_members goes through the domain method (group.add(user)), bypassing whatever GroupUser-level bookkeeping the domain path performs. Removal is the only membership operation that skips the join-model's lifecycle behavior; any bookkeeping maintained on GroupUser create/destroy (counter maintenance or later additions like title/primary-group cleanup) is silently skipped on this path, producing add/remove asymmetry that surfaces as stale derived state the next time someone relies on the domain method's side effects.

[ADVISORY] params[:visible] == "true" strict string comparison silently maps a JSON boolean true to false (same pattern at line 38 in update). An API client sending JSON {"visible": true} gets visible=false persisted with a 200 response; only form-encoded "true" string works, and nothing in the code or contract documents the string-only type, so integrations intermittently flip group visibility.

[ADVISORY] update repeats the params[:visible] == "true" strict string comparison that silently inverts JSON booleans. JSON API callers setting visible:true toggle the group to invisible with a success response; the same type-coercion trap as the create site, independently reachable.

[ADVISORY] add_members silently skips usernames that don't match a user (no strip, no per-username error reporting) and still returns success_json. An admin pasting 'bob, alice' (whitespace after comma) or a misspelled username gets a green success response while only the exactly-matching subset is added; the client's findMembers reload shows a partial result with no indication which names were dropped, so the admin has no signal the add failed.

[ADVISORY] limit and offset are unvalidated .to_i casts on a public endpoint: negative values produce invalid SQL OFFSET/LIMIT (500), and an arbitrarily large limit removes the row cap entirely. offset=-1 on /groups/:name/members raises a Postgres error surfaced as a 500 on a public page; limit=1000000 lets any visitor materialize an entire group's member set serialized in one response, re-opening the unbounded-materialization path this change was meant to close.

[ADVISORY] findMembers() is fire-and-forget in setupController (promise neither returned nor handled), replacing the old afterModel that blocked the transition, so the admin group page renders against the model's default user_count=0/offset=0 before any data arrives and AJAX failures are swallowed. The pagination controls briefly compute currentPage=0/totalPages=0 (showingLast true) from the defaults, and if the members request fails the admin sees a permanently empty member list with a '1/1' counter and no error — the failure mode the old transition-blocking shape surfaced is now silent.

[BUG] The update action switched from parsing the nested payload (params[:group][:name]/[:visible]/[:usernames]) to flat params and now unconditionally assigns group.visible = params[:visible] == "true", so legacy API clients that still send the old nested payload get visible silently flipped to false and their rename silently dropped while the endpoint returns 200 success_json. Any existing script/API consumer using the previously documented PUT /admin/groups/:id body {group: {name, visible, alias_level}} gets a 200 response but the group is made invisible (data change) and its name/membership changes are discarded with no error — a silent no-op/mis-op for out-of-tree callers introduced by this diff without any deprecation or versioning.

[BUG] The create action no longer reads params[:group][:name] or params[:group][:usernames], so legacy clients that create groups via the old nested payload now send an empty name (fails validation with an opaque 422) and can no longer create a group with initial members at all. Existing integrations that relied on POST /admin/groups with group[usernames] to provision populated groups now either fail with a validation error (nested name not parsed → name = '') or, if adapted to the flat shape, silently create empty groups — a removed capability and changed request contract with no acceptance or compatibility shim in this diff.

[BUG] The route get "users" under admin groups is deleted (replaced by put/delete "members"), removing the GET /admin/groups/:id/users endpoint that existed before this diff. Any consumer of the removed endpoint — scripts, API clients, or older deployed front-ends during rolling deploy — now receives a routing failure/404 where they previously received the member list; the endpoint was removed as a side effect of this fix with no replacement route for reads.

[BUG] The members action previously returned the full member list for non-automatic groups (the deleted TODO comment documented that unpaginated behavior as deliberate) but now applies limit=50/offset to every group, while app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs gained no pagination controls. Public group pages for any non-automatic group with more than 50 members now silently display only the first 50 members with no way for a regular user to see the rest — a user-visible truncation of information that the old code explicitly avoided, introduced silently by this diff.

[ADVISORY] The admin-group-selector component template was gutted to a bare unbound <input type="text">, deleting whatever bindings/behavior the component previously had, as an unrelated edit inside a membership-fix PR. Every admin surface that still renders {{admin-group-selector}} now shows a dead text input with no value binding or group resolution — whoever relies on that component silently loses its function with no error indicating why.

[ADVISORY] The member-adding UI is now only rendered inside {{#if id}}, so the previous flow of creating a new group together with its initial members (old template rendered user-selector unconditionally and createWithUsernames submitted them) is no longer possible. Admins who previously typed a name and usernames and hit save once must now create an empty group, wait for it to appear, then add members in a second step — a silently removed capability of the admin workflow that no iteration note or changelog marks as accepted.

[ADVISORY] findMembers() is now fire-and-forget in setupController (the awaited afterModel promise was removed), so the route renders immediately while user_count still holds its default 0. Every visit to the admin group page shows a flash of '0/0' pagination and an empty member list until the ajax resolves (same pattern in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6 lines 5-12 for the public page) — the previously guaranteed 'fully loaded or loading spinner' contract was silently replaced by a transient wrong-state render.

[BUG] The public members endpoint takes limit and offset straight from user params with no clamping, removing the previous hard cap of 200 rows for automatic groups and allowing arbitrarily large LIMIT values. A client passes limit=9999999 on any group that passes guardian.ensure_can_see! and forces the server to load and serialize the entire membership in one request — a memory/CPU amplification vector on large groups, and full member-list enumeration beyond the 200-row ceiling the old code imposed on automatic groups.

[ADVISORY] Negative values of limit or offset (params[:limit].to_i / params[:offset].to_i) are passed unvalidated into .limit(-1).offset(-1), which Postgres rejects ('LIMIT/OFFSET must not be negative'), producing an unhandled 500. Any anonymous or regular user can trigger a 500 with a crafted query string (e.g. ?offset=-1), generating error noise and log volume; the contract should return a 4xx for malformed pagination input.

[ADVISORY] add_members calls params.require(:usernames).split(",") without type-checking, so a request supplying usernames as an array (usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b or a JSON array body) raises NoMethodError: undefined method 'split' for Array and returns an unhandled 500. An admin (or any client tampering with parameter encoding) gets a raw 500 instead of a 4xx validation error; the failure is silent-server-error rather than a handled input-validation path, and the same array-shaped param is exactly what the client-side user-selector can naturally emit.

[ADVISORY] The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' test sends `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`, but remove_member is routed only via `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` (config/routes.rb) — the test's HTTP verb contradicts the route under test, while the sibling success test correctly uses `xhr :delete`. The assertion only holds because Rails functional tests dispatch by action name and ignore route verbs; the test documents and exercises a verb that does not exist for this endpoint, so anyone converting these specs to routing-honoring request specs (or trusting the spec to learn the API contract) is misled, and the test breaks the moment dispatch goes through the router.

[ADVISORY] The new automatic-group guard tests for add_members (line 83), remove_member (line 104), and update (line 51) all hardcode `group_id: 1` / `id: 1` and assume the seeded automatic group occupies id 1, instead of Fabricating an automatic group the way the .destroy tests in this same diff do. If automatic-group seeding in the test database ever changes (ids shift, seeds not loaded), these tests silently exercise a non-automatic group — add_members with the fake username 'l77t' would then silently succeed and the 422 assertion would fail confusingly, or worse, the remove_member assertion would guard the wrong group — and the failure message points nowhere near the real cause.

[ADVISORY] This diff deletes the PATCH-era tests that explicitly covered silent edge behavior ('succeeds silently when adding non-existent users', 'succeeds silently when removing non-members') but the replacement endpoints retain both behaviors untested: add_members skips nonexistent usernames via `if user = User.find_by_username(username)` (groups_controller.rb add_members) and remove_member's `group.users.delete(user_id)` silently no-ops for a non-member id. An admin who typos a username in the new Add-members input gets a 200 success response and the client reloads a member list that never grew — with no test in the diff asserting that silent-skip is intentional, a future refactor that makes a missing user raise (or partially apply) would pass CI while changing real admin-facing behavior.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten .update action introduces the `!group.automatic` rename branch, the `params[:alias_level].present?` branch, and the save-failure branch, but the only .update test in the diff covers the automatic-group path; no test renames a non-automatic group, sets alias_level, or triggers render_json_error, and the old coverage for updating a normal group (rename + members) was deleted with this change. A regression in the non-automatic rename or alias_level assignment (e.g., a typo making the guard `group.automatic` instead of `!group.automatic`, or alias_level no longer persisted) would pass this suite, since the sole update test asserts only that the automatic group's name is unchanged.

[BUG] update() switched from the nested `params[:group]` payload contract to flat top-level params in the same PR that changes the client, so old-payload requests are silently mis-parsed instead of being rejected. During a rolling deploy (and for any out-of-tree API consumer or cached-browser session still sending the old `{group: {name, visible, alias_level, usernames}}` shape), `params[:visible]` is nil so line 38 forces `group.visible = false` on every save, `params[:name]` is nil so name edits are silently dropped, and the `usernames` key is ignored entirely — the request returns 200 while the group's visibility is flipped and membership edits are lost.

[BUG] create() reads `params[:name]` at the top level while every pre-deploy client (cached admin JS and existing API scripts) POSTs the name nested under `params[:group][:name]`, and the old 'create group with initial usernames' capability is dropped with no replacement path. Old clients hitting the new create action get `params[:name]` nil, save a blank name, and receive a validation error — group creation breaks outright during the deploy window; additionally, any consumer that relied on seeding members at creation time can no longer do so (membership must now happen in a second PUT call, which old clients never make).

[BUG] The /groups/:name/members response shape changed from a bare serialized array to a `{members: [...], meta: {...}}` envelope, breaking any client that consumes the old shape as an array. A browser with cached pre-deploy JS (old group.js does `result.map(function(u) {...})` on the response) throws a TypeError on the group members page because an object has no `.map`, and out-of-tree API consumers parsing the endpoint as a JSON array get their integrations broken with no versioned fallback route.

[ADVISORY] The PATCH-based incremental membership contract (`changes: {add: [...], delete: [...]}`) is deleted outright in this diff with no deprecation period, alias route, or documentation of removal. Out-of-tree API consumers that PATCH membership changes now get update() which ignores `params[:changes]` entirely and returns 200 — their membership modifications silently no-op, and there is no error signal telling them the contract changed (silent public-surface change).

[BUG] totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which over-counts by one page whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit (should be ceil), so a group with exactly 50 members reports "1/2". An admin viewing a group with exactly 50 (or 100, 150...) members sees a next arrow that is enabled (showingLast compares currentPage 1 to totalPages 2 and finds them unequal); clicking it clamps offset to Math.min(0+50, 50) = 50, fetches a page the server renders as empty, and the admin is left staring at an empty member list labeled page 2/2.

[BUG] The next/previous actions mutate group.offset optimistically before findMembers resolves, with no in-flight guard and no rollback on failure. Double-clicking next issues two overlapping requests (the second reads the already-advanced offset), and whichever response arrives last wins, so the member list and offset can end up describing different pages; if the ajax request fails, offset stays advanced, currentPage increments, and the UI permanently shows a page number that does not match the members on screen with no error surfaced.

[BUG] setupController calls model.findMembers() as a fire-and-forget statement, dropping the promise that the removed afterModel hook previously returned, so the fetch's rejection is unhandled and the transition reports success before any members load. If the /groups/:name/members.json request fails (500, network error, permission change), the admin group page renders with an empty member list and zero indication of failure — the failure is invisible; the previous code blocked rendering on the promise and let the route's error path handle rejection.

[BUG] Same regression as the admin route: setupController calls model.findMembers() without returning or catching the promise, replacing afterModel's awaited version. On the public group members page, a failed members request leaves the table permanently empty with no error shown to the user, and the rejection propagates as an unhandled promise rejection instead of the route error handling the afterModel version exercised.

[BUG] removeMember and addMembers attach only a .then handler with no .catch, and the reload inside .then (self.findMembers()) is not returned, so every failure in the mutation chain — the DELETE/PUT itself or the follow-up reload — is an unhandled rejection. An admin who clicks the remove (×) icon or Add and the request fails (422 for automatic groups via API race, 404, 500) sees the bootbox confirm succeed and then nothing happens: no error message, member list unchanged, failure completely invisible; the controller's addMembers/removeMember actions (admin-group.js.es6 lines 51-65) also discard the returned promise, so even a caller-level catch would not help.

[BUG] add_members silently skips usernames that do not resolve to a user (User.find_by_username returns nil and the block just continues) and then renders success_json based on group.save, reporting HTTP 200 while dropping part or all of the requested membership work. A request to add "bob,jane" where one username was deleted since selection (or contains stray whitespace, since split(",") is not stripped) returns success while adding only a subset or nothing; the client reloads the member list, so the admin sees the member didn't appear but receives no error identifying which usernames were dropped.

[ADVISORY] remove_member performs group.users.delete(user_id) — an immediate, unconditional join-table deletion — and only then uses group.save's result to decide the response, diverging from the previous code path that called group.remove(user). If group.save fails validation after the deletion has already been committed, the API returns an error while the removal has actually taken effect (reported failure over completed work); and the raw association delete bypasses whatever GroupUser destroy-callback maintenance (e.g. user_count bookkeeping) the Group#remove path performed, so the next admin group index render can show a stale user_count.

[ADVISORY] The public members endpoint accepts an unbounded limit param — (params[:limit] || 50).to_i has no maximum — and applies it before serialization with no cap. Any user who can see a group can pass limit=100000000 and force the server to load and serialize the entire membership in one response, exhausting memory/bandwidth on the request path; the new code is an improvement over the old no-limit non-automatic path, but the newly introduced cap mechanism still lacks an upper clamp.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] add_members silently skips usernames that do not resolve to a user (User.find_by_username returns nil and the block just continues) and then renders success_json based on group.save, reporting HTTP 200 while dropping part or all of the requested membership work. A request to add "bob,jane" where one username was deleted since selection (or contains stray whitespace, since split(",") is not stripped) returns success while adding only a subset or nothing; the client reloads the member list, so the admin sees the member didn't appear but receives no error identifying which usernames were dropped.

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, usernames are split on "," and iterated without stripping whitespace, and missing users are silently ignored: `if user = User.find_by_username(username) ... end`. After the loop it returns `success_json` solely based on `group.save`, which will succeed even if zero users were added (e.g., all usernames invalid/whitespace). Thus the endpoint can return HTTP 200 while partially or fully failing to perform the requested membership additions, with no indication of which usernames were skipped.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] remove_member performs group.users.delete(user_id) — an immediate, unconditional join-table deletion — and only then uses group.save's result to decide the response, diverging from the previous code path that called group.remove(user). If group.save fails validation after the deletion has already been committed, the API returns an error while the removal has actually taken effect (reported failure over completed work); and the raw association delete bypasses whatever GroupUser destroy-callback maintenance (e.g. user_count bookkeeping) the Group#remove path performed, so the next admin group index render can show a stale user_count.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code executes `group.users.delete(user_id)` (which immediately deletes the join record) and only afterward uses `group.save` to decide whether to return success or `render_json_error` (diff: `group.users.delete(user_id)` then `if group.save ... else ...`). Since the removal has already been committed, a failing `group.save` would yield an error response even though the member was removed. Also, this bypasses the previous membership-removal path (`group.remove(user)` used elsewhere in the old controller logic), which could skip any removal-specific callbacks/maintenance that method performed; the diff itself confirms the bypass even if the exact callbacks aren’t shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The public members endpoint accepts an unbounded limit param — (params[:limit] || 50).to_i has no maximum — and applies it before serialization with no cap. Any user who can see a group can pass limit=100000000 and force the server to load and serialize the entire membership in one response, exhausting memory/bandwidth on the request path; the new code is an improvement over the old no-limit non-automatic path, but the newly introduced cap mechanism still lacks an upper clamp.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff introduces pagination parameters but does not clamp `limit`: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then `group.users...limit(limit)` (with `total = group.users.count`). Any requester who can hit `/groups/:group_id/members` can pass an arbitrarily large `limit` and force the server to load and serialize a huge membership set in one response. While the default is now 50, the lack of a maximum is directly visible in the new code path and matches the finding’s DoS/memory/bandwidth concern.
